Subject: Scheduling challenge for a multi‑mode project under shared resources and a fixed budget

Team,

This memo outlines the scheduling challenge for our upcoming project. We must establish a feasible and efficient baseline plan that selects one execution option for each activity, sequences the work to avoid resource conflicts, respects all dependency and timing rules, and keeps total execution spending within the approved budget. The detailed counts, limits, and data references are provided in the Annex.

Context and scope
- The project comprises multiple interdependent activities that share renewable resource types with fixed capacities.
- Each activity can be delivered in one of several execution modes. Modes represent different ways of doing the work (for example, allocating more personnel or equipment to finish sooner) and trade off speed, resource usage, and direct cost.
- The objective is to complete the entire project as quickly as possible while satisfying all constraints and staying within the funding cap.

Execution modes and non‑preemption
- Exactly one execution mode must be selected for each activity.
- Each mode has its own duration, resource requirements, and cost; faster modes are available at a higher cost and may draw more resources.
- Activities are non‑preemptive: once an activity starts in a chosen mode, it runs to completion without interruption.

Dependencies and timing controls
- Precedence relationships specify which activities must finish before others can start.
- Some predecessor–successor links impose minimum delays (the successor must wait at least a specified time after the predecessor finishes).
- A subset of links also impose maximum delays (the successor must start within a specified time after the predecessor finishes).
- In addition, some activities have earliest allowed start times (release dates), and some have hard deadlines by which they must be completed.

Resource environment and conservative safety rule
- Resources are renewable. When an activity finishes, the resources it used return to the pool and can be reassigned.
- To manage risk in a simple and robust way, we apply a conservative safety rule for activities that are not directly related by a precedence link:
  If there exists even one pair of mode choices (one for each activity) and at least one resource for which their combined usage would exceed that resource’s capacity, then those two activities cannot run at the same time and must be sequenced (one finishes before the other starts).
- This is the only resource limitation applied. There is no separate “at all times” capacity check beyond these pairwise sequencing decisions. Practically, this means that even if some combinations of mode choices would fit concurrently, the possibility of overload in any combination requires us to avoid overlap and decide which activity goes first.

Budget constraint
- The project budget is fixed. The sum of the costs of the selected execution modes across all activities must not exceed this amount. This budget is non‑renewable and applies to the entire project.

Planning implications
- The scheduling team must balance competing drivers: choosing faster (costlier) modes to compress the timeline versus slower (cheaper) modes to protect the budget.
- Minimum and maximum delay requirements reduce flexibility in sequencing and may force certain activities onto or near the critical path.
- Release dates and hard deadlines further constrain start and finish windows.
- The conservative resource safety rule can reduce parallelism among otherwise independent activities, so careful ordering is required to avoid unnecessary idle time while maintaining compliance.
- If the combination of deadlines, maximum delays, and budget limits forces infeasible trade‑offs, we will surface options (e.g., adjusting timing windows, revisiting mode costs, or increasing capacities/budget) for decision.

Goal and expected outcome
- Build a feasible schedule that assigns a single mode to every activity, sequences work to satisfy the conservative resource rule, honors all dependencies, release dates, and deadlines, and keeps total mode costs within the approved budget.
- Among all feasible plans, we seek the one with the shortest overall completion time.
